'''Marianne the Vault scholar''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Marianne is a scholarly individual who resides in Vault 33.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===Season 1===
====[[The Head]]====
Sitting at her desk, Marianne unlocks the door from her computer for [[Norm MacLean|Norm]], who delivers a tray of food for the [[Vault 32 raider]]s. As Marianne opens the door hatch to the raider's room, she passes the trays of food to them all while trying to be polite to them all. 

When a conference is held led by the Vault 33 governing council members [[Woody Thomas|Woody]], [[Reg McPhee|Reg]], and [[Betty Pearson|Betty]]. The topic of the discussion is what to do with the Vault 32 raiders and when it's decided to integrate them into their society. When [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] suggests teaching the Vault 32 raiders [[William Shakespeare|Shakespeare]] and when they're ready, [[Christopher Marlowe|Marlowe]]. However, Marianne cuts in, stating that Shakespeare is too advanced for them, and suggests starting with a more moral framework with [[Immanuel Kant|Kant]], [[John Stuart Mill|Mill]], etc.

After a couple more suggestions are tossed out, Norm scoffs and Reg asks him if he has a suggestion, which he notes that it's not

Mind-controlled slave |TV actor =[[Casey Hendershot]] }} The '''massive legionary''' is a character who appears in the [[Fallout TV series season 2|second season]] of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Background== The massive legionary is a member of [[Caesar's Legion]] in 2296. He appears to carry an intense hatred for the [[New California Republic]] as an enemy of the Legion, to the point of even disregarding other hostiles. At some point, [[Hank MacLean]]'s mind-controlled [[X-Branch office worker|workers]] would capture him, along with NCR holdout [[Biff (TV series)|Ranger Biff]], and install both with [[Brain-computer interface chip]]s, though the chips were kept inactive, waiting for his orders.{{FOTV|2|6}} The chips on both men were activated by Lucy to prevent the legionary from killing Biff, and the legionary subsequently became another of Hank's friendly and docile office workers. His presence seemingly served a double purpose to convince Lucy that Hank's technology would be the only way to stop the Legion from invading New Vegas.{{FOTV|2|7}

{{Infobox character |games =FOTV |image =FOTV Vault 31 Cryobay.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |family = |location =[[Vault 31]] |role =Junior executive |affiliation =[[Vault 31]]/[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] |TV actor = |dod = |dod verified= }} '''Maximillian Dottino''' is a pre-War junior executive of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] who is currently preserved in [[Vault 31]]. ==Background== Dottino was a Vault-Tec junior employee selected to participate in [[Bud Askins]]' executive assistant training program "[[Bud's Buds]]," a plan to create "super managers" who would define the future of humanity after the [[Great War]] wiped out all competitors to Vault-Tec. Dottino and the other Buds would be kept in [[Cryonics|cryostasis]] in Vault 31, periodically thawed out and transferred to [[Vault 32]] or [[Vault 33|33]] to manage the dwellers and participate in controlled breeding (eugenics), all under Askins' supervision.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So what's Vault 32 and 33? Just people to be controlled?"''
[[Bud Askins]]: ''"What? No! When you put it like that, it sounds downright morally questionable. They're our breeding pool, the ultimate expression of HR R&D. Genetically selected to breed with my Buds to create a class of super managers. People with positivity, people who make lemonade. People who will inherit the Earth after we've wiped the surface clean."''
